examples.pie: suHnús wiHrṓy ǵn̥h₁yéto. nu h₁ím déwsbʰis sléh₂gʷt bʰéh₂t-kʷe. tébʰye h₁nómn̥ dʰéh₁oh₂. téwe h₁nómn̥ méǵh₂ h₁syéh₁t téwe-kʷe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁syéh₁t. déywōs h₁ím ph₂sté. nu deywṓs h₁ím ḱléwsont.
examples.en: A son was born to the hero. He took him in his arms and said, "I shall give you a name." "May your name be great, and may your fame be imperishable. Gods, protect him." Then the gods heard him.

examples.pie: nu nókʷts gʷémt wiḱpótis-kʷe légʰt. bʰór wiḱpóteys lewbʰéh₂m dʰwórm̥ mē gʷm̥yés. téwe h₃ókʷih₁ mē widóyh₁tām. nu bʰór téwe dóws ḱr̥mh₂yéh₁t. ḱwṓ bʰéwdʰeti deywós-kʷe ḱóymom péh₂sti. h₁yós gʷṓs stéh₂yeti só mr̥yéh₁t.
examples.en: Night has come, and the master has lain down. Thief, do not come to the master's dear door! Let your eyes not see. Now, thief, let your arm go slack. The dog is awake, and the god guards the home. Whoever steals the cattle, let him die.

examples.pie: méh₂ter spéḱye. snéygʷʰeti. téḱnom snígʷʰm̥ dedórḱh₂e. ǵʰéyōm gʷegʷóme. snígʷʰi lóygōh₂. lóyge dṓm-kʷe mē léykʷs. nékʷti gólēti.

examples.pie: nu wos déywōs ḱóm ugʷsénm̥ dedh₃més. mórom stégesbʰos h₂pó sl̥h₂gʷté. h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs mr̥yóntor sénōs mr̥yóntor. ń̥mr̥tōs nos mē gʰrémete. móros-ge nos póyḱons gʷh₂yéh₁t.
examples.en: Gods, now we give you this ox. Take the plague away from the houses! The young are dying, the old ones are dying. Immortals, do not rage at us! May the plague indeed go to our enemies.

source.name: coinage
source.note: kʷéyteti 'notice, attend to' (Ved. cétati) in the sense its Balto-Slavic relatives gave the root: OCS čьtǫ, čisti 'count, read' and Lith. skaitýti 'count, read' (LIV² s.v. *kʷei̯t-). No PIE verb 'count' reconstructs: *h₂rey- has only nouns ('number': OIr. rím, OE rīm, Gk ἀριθμός; Kroonen 2013 s.v. *rīma-), and Lat. reor (*reh₁-) is Latin only (LIV²).
